paragraphs.source_en: He said that for the second meeting they meant to invite a number of well-known literary men and hold a grand gathering, and he said to me, 'I do hope you too will honor us with your presence.' I asked him, 'Are you doing another Chikamatsu domestic play?' He said, 'No, next time we have chosen something quite new; we have decided on The Golden Demon.' Then I asked him, 'In that case, what part have you been given?' He said, 'I am Miss Omiya.' Kochi playing Miss Omiya, how amusing that will be! I am determined to attend and applaud him.' Kangetsu said with a strained, ambiguous smile, 'It should be amusing, shouldn't it?' Linking together Andrea del Sarto, the peacock's tongue, and the matter of 'tochimenbo,' the master said in retaliation, 'Still, that fellow is a good man. He is honest and has not a frivolous bone in him. He is altogether different from someone like Meitei.' Mr. Meitei seemed not to mind in the least, and laughed. 'After all, the likes of me will always be a Gyotoku chopping board.' The master said, 'I suppose that is about what you are.' In truth, the master had no idea what the phrase 'Gyotoku chopping board' meant; but, having spent many years as a teacher and become expert at bluffing, he now applied his classroom experience to social intercourse. Kangetsu, however, asked quite frankly, 'What does that "Gyotoku chopping board" mean?' The master looked toward the alcove and said, 'Those narcissi are ones I bought on my way home from the bath at the end of last year and put in that vase. Look, they have lasted a long time, haven't they?' By this means the master forcibly smothered the question of the 'Gyotoku chopping board.' Meitei, twirling the stem of his pipe on his fingertips like a performer of daikagura, said, 'Speaking of the year's end, at the end of last year I had a truly strange experience.' The master, looking relieved as though he had cast the 'Gyotoku chopping board' far behind him, said, 'What sort of experience was it? Tell us about it at once.' The strange experience that Mr. Meitei had undergone was as follows:
